title: feat(router): add worker cache-reuse telemetry (F2-F5)
body:
## Summary

Adds always-on cache-reuse counters for each KV-routing attempt. The router records the raw cached prefix on the best eligible worker and on the selected worker/rank. The worker reports its cache-hit counts when the request completes. Routing decisions and tier weights are unchanged; reported token values are raw and uncapped.

The counters use the existing `RouterRequestMetrics` and request-guard lifecycle, with one once-only flag for completion, errors, cancellation, and dropped streams. This incorporates Neelay's reference cleanup from #15173, retaining counters rather than introducing histograms.

## Metrics and compatibility

All names below have the `dynamo_component_router_` prefix and carry `phase` (`aggregated`, `prefill`, or `decode`) and `model` labels.

| Measurement | Metric |
| --- | --- |
| Received input tokens (F0) | `input_sequence_tokens_sum` (existing histogram sum) |
| Best eligible cached prefix (F2) | `kv_best_eligible_cached_prefix_tokens_total` |
| Selected worker/rank cached prefix (F3) | `kv_selected_cached_prefix_tokens_total` |
| Worker lookup hits, when available (F4) | `kv_worker_lookup_tokens_total` |
| Backend-reported cache-hit tokens (F5) | `kv_worker_reused_tokens_total` |
| Worker reporting coverage | `kv_worker_outcomes_total{result}` |

- F0's existing histogram now excludes query-only selections and carries matching phase/model labels. Queries needing process-wide totals must sum across those labels.
- F2/F3 are recorded at selection. Worker values require successful completion and a valid prompt-matched report. The guard retains the attempt's original phase.
- Missing external lookup data does not fall back to successful hits or zero. F5 is still recorded, F4 is not incremented, and the outcome is `lookup_unavailable`. A valid lookup report is `complete`; missing, invalid, overflowing, or failed reports are `incomplete`.
- Both the vLLM worker and router now use `engine_data.kv_cache_hit`. No compatibility reader for the old key is included; upgrade frontends and workers together.
- F2–F5 need no enable flag. F1 history tracking remains separate and opt-in in #14889.

## Interpretation and limitations

- Compare the same model and phase. Prefill and decode are separate routing attempts; migration adds attempts that may include already-generated tokens. Selection and completion happen at different times.
- Multimodal routing tokens can differ from the input token IDs counted by F0.
- Existing `router_kv_hit_rate` is tier-weighted; these counters are not.
- Worker reporting is currently vLLM-only. SGLang and TensorRT-LLM KV attempts record router estimates and incomplete worker outcomes. Extending worker reporting to non-KV routing is deferred.
- Stock vLLM does not expose a separate external lookup count. Its cached-token statistics may also retain initial matches after transfer failures. F5 is a backend report, not independently verified successful reuse; backend failure-accounting work is separate.

title: feat(profiler): DGDC reconcile-diff algorithm
body:
## Summary

Adds the reconcile-diff algorithm for DGDC lifecycle management — [tracking issue #13545](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13545), item 5 ("materialize DGDCs, and reconcile their lifecycle"). Given a desired set of candidates and the current set of DGDCs, decides what to create, delete, and update.

## Key design decision

Identity is a **content hash** of the rendered spec + evaluation-context fields, not `Status.Rank`. Rank changes over time as better candidates are found and worse ones evicted, often with no change to the candidate's own content — using it as identity would force unnecessary delete+recreate churn. Using a content hash instead means a real content change and an identity change are the same event, which lines up naturally with `DynamoGraphDeploymentCandidate.Spec`'s real, confirmed CEL immutability rule (`"spec is immutable"`) — there's no "update spec" code path in this module at all.

Confirmed against the real `v1beta2` Go types (fetched directly from the `#13603` PR branch)

title: feat(profiler): bounded scalar/Pareto candidate selector
body:
## Summary
 
Implements "select bounded scalar/Pareto results" — [tracking issue #13545](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13545), item 5. 
Given the current selection and one newly-scored `Candidate`, returns the updated selection. Maintaining state across a stream of candidates is the caller's job — same design as `compute_actions` in the DGDC reconcile-diff work (`#14931`).
 
## What's confirmed, not assumed
 
- `Candidate.objectives` is a dict keyed by `OptimizationTarget` value.
- Each objective's maximize/minimize direction is a **search-level** property (`[(t.value, t.maximize) for t in resolved_pareto_objectives]`), not a per-candidate field — callers supply it via `ObjectiveSpec`, one per objective, at the goal level.
- Scalar goals break score ties by fewer GPUs: *"rank (best score, ties → fewer GPUs) for every scalar goal."* Implemented exactly, with dedicated tests for both the tie-break firing and *not* firing when it shouldn't.
- Pareto results are *"only non-dominated candidates."*
- `ParetoGoal.max_candidates` defaults to `5`, matching the real, confirmed `RecommendationSpec.MaxCandidates` default on the `v1beta2` DGDR type (fetched directly from the `#13603` PR branch).
## Eviction policy
 
NSGA-II crowding distance when the front exceeds `max_candidates` — the standard algorithm for this exact problem, not an arbitrary rule. Boundary candidates (best on any single objective) get infinite distance by construction and are never evicted; eviction thins dense interior clusters instead of trimming the front's own extremes.

title: fix(kv-router): break request-lease observer ownership cycle
body:
## Overview:

`KvRouter::new` hands the scheduler a strong `Arc` to the `RequestLeaseManager` as its replica observer, and the manager holds the scheduler's `SchedulerBookingCleanup` handle that it receives from `set_scheduler`. Both edges are strong, so neither side can drop once construction has wired them. A router that fails to construct after that point, or one that is dropped, leaks its scheduler actor and lease state. This PR replaces the strong observer with a weak one so the cycle is broken while callbacks still reach the manager for as long as it is alive.

This is the first of three independent PRs split out of #14965. That PR's Mooncake Store test for failed router construction depends on `RequestLeaseManager::replica_observer` from this change. The leak itself exists on `main` today and is not specific to Mooncake Store.

## Details:

- Add `RequestLeaseManager::replica_observer`, which returns an `Arc<dyn ReplicaRequestLeaseObserver>` backed by a `Weak<RequestLeaseManagerInner>`.
- Replace the `impl ReplicaRequestLeaseObserver for RequestLeaseManager` with a private `WeakRequestLeaseObserver`. Each of `admitted`, `progressed`, and `completed` upgrades the weak reference and forwards to the existing `register_remote`, `touch_booking`, and `complete_remote` methods, or becomes a no-op once the manager is gone.
- `KvRouter::new` passes `request_leases.replica_observer()` to the scheduler instead of `Some(Arc::new(request_leases.clone()))`.
- Add the regression test `replica_observer_forwards_live_callbacks_without_retaining_manager`. It admits a booking on a tracked router, drives the three callbacks through the observer and checks the lease record at each step, drops the router, and asserts the manager is released. It then calls the callbacks again on the dangling observer to confirm they are no-ops.
- Make the `tracked_router` test helper in `kv_router.rs` `pub(super)` so the `request_lease` test module can reuse it.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/llm/src/kv_router/request_lease.rs`: `replica_observer` and `WeakRequestLeaseObserver`, then the new test at the top of the `tests` module.
- `lib/llm/src/kv_router.rs`: the one-line change in `KvRouter::new` where the observer is handed to the scheduler.

## Validation

```
cargo test -p dynamo-llm --no-default-features --lib -- kv_router::request_lease
```

Both tests in the module pass. The regression test was also run against the previous strong observer in a throwaway worktree, where the `manager.upgrade().is_none()` assertion fails, so the test does detect the cycle. `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean.

title: feat(power-agent): gate pod readiness on cap enforcement
body:
Implements [DEP #14767](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/14767), following the execute-ready implementation design posted in that issue's comments.

## Summary

Today a PowerAgent pod has no readiness probe, so it is Ready from the moment its container starts and stays Ready while every reconcile cycle fails. `kubectl get pods` shows `1/1 Running` for an agent that has enforced nothing since startup, and `kubectl rollout status` reports success for a rollout of non-functional agents.

This makes pod readiness mean that the agent is enforcing power caps. The claim published is narrow and self-reported:

> The agent's last reconcile cycle completed every enforcement action it was required to take with no reported failure, and completed recently.

A GPU with no running workload is intentionally skipped, so the claim covers the actions the cycle was required to take, not the live state of every GPU on the node.

### 1. The actuator reports whether its writes actually landed

`apply_cap` returns a `CapWriteResult(effective_w, ok)` NamedTuple instead of a bare int. `effective_w` keeps the existing contract exactly — the post-clamp value the agent *intended* to apply, returned regardless of the write's outcome. `ok` is the new information.

This could not be fixed at the call site by inspecting the return value: both actuators catch their write errors, increment `apply_failures_total`, and return a plausible post-clamp wattage anyway, so **a clean return from `apply_cap` was never evidence that a cap is live.** A `NamedTuple` specifically, so every existing wattage consumer has to be edited rather than silently keep working against a value that now means something else.

On the DCGM side five distinct early returns leave the GPU unwritten and now report `ok=False`; only the `_apply_cap_inner` normal return issued a Set. `_apply_cap_inner`, `restore_default`, and `restore_default_by_uuid` are unchanged — the last already returned `Optional[bool]` with exactly the semantics needed.

### 2. `reconcile_once()` folds that into a whole-cycle enforcement boolean

True iff every enforcement action the cycle was required to take completed, and the inputs it depended on were obtained. Every path that currently swallows a failure to keep the loop running now drives it false: a failed cap write, a cap skipped on unconfirmed GPU identity or mid-write re-enumeration, a failed PID snapshot, a failed release, a failed pod list, a failed device-count refresh.

**The runtime behaviour of those paths is unchanged** — the agent still never drops caps on failure, and a failing cycle does not exit the process (a NotReady agent that keeps reconciling can recover, while a restart drops in-memory GPU ownership). What changes is that the outcome is now observable as *state* rather than only as a counter.

Two things stay deliberately outside the fold:

- The persistence-only retries in `_flush_pending_retirements` / `_flush_pending_acquisitions`. Each retries a durable record whose hardware write and in-memory ownership already succeeded, so live enforcement is correct and only a *restarted* agent would notice.
- A cgroup read that yields no pod UID, which is indistinguishable from a non-Kubernetes process and so is not a failure the cycle can observe at all.

Two details the tests pin explicitly:

- The fold is `_reconcile_gpu(...) and ok`, never `ok and _reconcile_gpu(...)` — the second form short-circuits, so once one GPU failed no later GPU would be reconciled.
- Both `_shutdown` short-circuits return the fold accumulated so far, never a literal `True`. An unconditional `True` would publish a fresh successful timestamp at the exact moment `_shutdown_cleanup` starts restoring default caps, so `/readyz` would claim enforcement while enforcement was being torn down.

### 3. A fixed `GET /readyz` on container port 8081

Backed by one monotonic float, `_last_good_cycle`, assigned exactly once per cycle after the `try` — so a reader on the server thread cannot see a torn mix, an exception cannot leave a stale *successful* timestamp in place, and no lock is required. `0.0` covers both "no cycle has ever succeeded" and "the last one failed".

Ready iff that timestamp is non-zero and younger than `STALE_AFTER_S = 3 * RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S` (45 s at the default). The staleness bound is what catches a *hung* cycle, which nothing else can: `run()` has no watchdog, NVML and DCGM calls are unbounded, and the probe's `failureThreshold` cannot see a blocked cycle because nothing is failing — the timestamp is simply not advancing. The bound restarts nothing. The multiplier of 3 tolerates a healthy cycle lasting up to `2 * RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S`, since `run()` sleeps *after* each cycle.

Served from its own `wsgiref` server on a daemon thread, deliberately **not** from the Prometheus server, which `--prometheus-port=0` disables — readiness must not be optional. Started before `run()`'s `try` so a bind failure propagates uncaught and the pod CrashLoops, rather than sending a never-enforcing agent through the full `_shutdown_cleanup` restore sweep. The response body carries the age (`ok last_good_cycle_age_s=3.2`), which is what makes a 503 diagnosable with `kubectl exec ... curl` and no log access.

### 4. Chart

The DaemonSet gains the `readyz` container port and a `readinessProbe` against it. Probe values are hard-coded rather than templated: the port is fixed in the agent with no CLI flag, so a chart value that could disagree with it is a footgun, and a configurable `failureThreshold` would let an operator dial the debounce until readiness means nothing.

No liveness probe, no `startupProbe`, `updateStrategy` untouched, `dev-pod.yaml` unchanged.

Chart `1.3.1` → `1.4.0` and `appVersion` `"1.2.0"` → `"1.3.0"`: the `/readyz` server is new runtime code in the image, so **chart >=1.4.0 requires image >=v1.3.0** — an older image has no `/readyz`, so every pod is permanently NotReady and the rollout stalls at the first node.

### Behavioural change for existing installs

Documented in `NOTES.txt` and the `daemonset.updateStrategy` comment block (there is no `README.md` under the chart):

> Power Agent pods now carry a readiness probe tied to cap enforcement. An agent that is not enforcing goes NotReady, which consumes the DaemonSet rollout budget under `rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: 1` and can stall a `helm upgrade` that previously completed. This is intended — an upgrade rolling over a node whose agent is not enforcing should not be reported as progress. The update strategy itself is unchanged.

### Out of scope

Per the DEP: no liveness probe, no operator / CRD / DGD-status / Planner change, no update-strategy change, no post-write readback, no per-pod enforcement records.

## Validation

**Python unit tests** — `pytest tests/` in `deploy/power-agent`: **359 passed**, 40 of them new. (These run in the Docker `test` stage, so a failure breaks the CI `--target test` build.)

- New `tests/test_readiness.py` (13 tests): 503 before the first successful cycle, 200 immediately after one, 503 once `STALE_AFTER_S` elapses; an unexpected exception from `reconcile_once` resets the timestamp so `/readyz` is 503 on the *next* poll rather than after the staleness bound, and the process does not terminate; a healthy cycle exceeding `2 * RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S` yields 503 (so the budget cannot be silently changed by a future interval or bound edit); stepping the wall clock neither extends nor expires readiness; `/readyz` serves with `--prometheus-port=0`; a pre-bound wildcard `("", 8081)` makes startup fatal and `_shutdown_cleanup` does *not* run; probe traffic emits no per-request log line.
- `tests/test_reconcile_failsafe.py`: every swallowed-failure path driving the boolean false, the no-short-circuit regression (a failure on GPU 0 still reconciles GPUs 1…N), the idle-GPU and `safe_default_watts`-fallback non-failures, and each `_release_managed_gpu` exit including the stale-projection skip.
- `tests/test_shutdown.py`: the fast path returns `True` (the only reachable result there), and the mid-loop break returns `True` when nothing had failed and `False` when a GPU already had.
- `tests/test_apply_cap.py` / `tests/test_dcgm_actuator.py`: a write whose NVML Set raised reports `ok=False` with a plausible `effective_w`; all five DCGM non-write exits report `ok=False` and assert no `dcgmConfigSet` was issued.
- `tests/test_pending_persistence.py`: a failed persistence-only retry leaves the cycle boolean `True`.
- Call-site migration: consumers read `.effective_w` (including the real-hardware `e2e_actuator_parity.py`, which subtracts the two actuators' returns and would otherwise raise `TypeError` on a GPU node long after CI went green), and actuator doubles now produce a real `CapWriteResult` via a shared `tests/actuator_double.py` — a bare `MagicMock` would make `reconcile_once` return a truthy `MagicMock`, the one migration class that fails silently.

**Helm** — new `deploy/helm/charts/power-agent/tests/readiness_probe_test.yaml` asserts the rendered probe values, the `readyz` container port, the unchanged `metrics` port, and the absence of a `livenessProbe`. **Not executed locally** (no `helm` binary on the authoring machine); the YAML parses and CI runs the suite.

**Lint** — `pre-commit run --files <changed>`: all hooks pass.

**Not asserted, deliberately**, per the DEP: that one failing cycle cannot make the pod NotReady. That is not a property this design has — `failureThreshold: 3` counts polls, not cycles — and a test claiming it would encode a false guarantee.

title: fix(backends): report cached-token usage during vLLM and SGLang streaming
body:
## Summary

Expose engine-reported cached-token usage before generation finishes in the vLLM and SGLang token-streaming adapters, without repeating unchanged usage metadata on every backend chunk.

Previously, both adapters attached `completion_usage` only at completion. Continuous-usage clients could receive generated-token totals but no cache details before then, including when they disconnected early.

Closes #14850 (vLLM) and #14938 (SGLang).

## Implementation

- Both adapters emit usage on the first usable report per choice, when prompt/cache metadata changes, and at completion. Explicit zero and unavailable cache counts remain distinct.
- vLLM maintains an O(1) request-wide cumulative completion total, advancing it as each choice is emitted so snapshots do not include later, un-emitted choices.
- SGLang captures usage before metadata-upload cleanup clears engine metadata and continues treating incomplete usage as optional.
- The Rust frontend already retains prompt/cache metadata and counts generated token IDs. A regression test verifies persistence and counting across sparse reports and interleaved choices.
- The optional Python vLLM and SGLang chat processors now retain sparse usage metadata and count generated tokens locally. Intermediate usage requires both `include_usage` and `continuous_usage_stats`; existing terminal/non-streaming usage behavior is retained. Metadata survives suppressed deltas and SGLang batched flushes.

For the synthetic 1,024-chunk, stable-cache example discussed in review, additional non-final MessagePack usage payload decreases from 114,194 bytes to 110 bytes (99.9%). This is an encoded-payload calculation, not a throughput or CPU benchmark.

## Reviewer entry points

- `components/src/dynamo/vllm/handlers.py`: `BaseWorkerHandler.generate_tokens`
- `components/src/dynamo/sglang/request_handlers/llm/decode_handler.py`: `_process_token_stream`

title: fix(trtllm): enable forward-pass metrics via the shared FPM opt-in
body:
## Summary

Relates to #14121.

`--publish-kv-events` turned on TensorRT-LLM's `enable_iter_perf_stats`. KV
events never read those statistics, and collecting them costs per-iteration
throughput a KV-router benchmark should not pay. Iteration statistics now
follow only the two switches that consume them.

| Switch | Prometheus `trtllm_*` | `enable_iter_perf_stats` | Worker-load sample | Forward-pass metrics | KV events |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--publish-kv-events` | no | no | no | no | yes |
| `--publish-metrics` | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| `--fpm-trace` / `DYN_FORWARDPASS_METRIC_PORT` | no | yes | yes | yes | no |

`--publish-metrics` keeps every path it had. `--fpm-trace` and
`DYN_FORWARDPASS_METRIC_PORT`, the opt-in vLLM and SGLang already use, enable
the Planner's forward-pass metrics without the Prometheus surface. The
resolution lives in `Config.validate`, so `enable_iter_perf_stats` and the
Publisher's two gates read one derived value.

The worker-load sample (used KV blocks per attention-DP rank) comes from the
same stats stream, so it is published whenever iteration statistics are on. The
KV router's per-worker scoring never reads it: `worker_logit` in
`lib/kv-router/src/scheduling/selector/default.rs` takes its overlap term from
KV events and its load term from the router's own active-sequence tracking. The
sample's one consumer is the optional `--active-decode-blocks-threshold` check
in `lib/llm/src/discovery/worker_monitor.rs`, where it is OR-ed with the
router's own decode-block estimate; a worker that trips the latch is published
through `set_overloaded_instances` and drops out of both the KV scheduler's
eligibility filter and the free pool until it recovers.

The sample gets no gate of its own because that check is already opt-in and
already fed by the router's own estimate — `kv_total_blocks` comes from the
runtime config, not from the metrics stream — so `--publish-metrics` adds an
engine-truth signal to an existing check rather than creating one. #14121's
concern was that scraping `/metrics` moves routing; publication here is
push-based from the stats thread, so a scrape is not the mechanism, and the
scoring path never reads the sample.

One test fix rides along: the TRT-LLM metrics E2E counted unique metric *names*
and accepted a zero block count, so it went green with either metric path
broken. It now requires an observation on each path separately.

## Validation

Run locally (no GPU, no TRT-LLM container on this host):

- `components/src/dynamo/trtllm/tests/test_trtllm_fpm_publisher.py` and
  `test_trtllm_prometheus_utils.py`: 63 passed, with the Rust bindings and
  `tensorrt_llm` stubbed. The gating tests cover each switch alone:
  `--publish-metrics` starts the stats thread, the forward-pass opt-in starts
  the stats thread and `FpmDirectPublisher`, `--publish-kv-events` starts no
  stats thread, nothing on starts no thread.
- `parse_args` under the same stubs: `publish_forward_pass_metrics` is true for
  `--fpm-trace`, `DYN_FORWARDPASS_METRIC_PORT` and `--publish-metrics`, and
  false for `--publish-kv-events` alone.
- Mutation-checked both gates. Dropping `self.publish_metrics or` from
  `Config.validate` flips `--publish-metrics` to no FPM; reverting the
  Publisher's FPM gate to `publish_metrics` fails two tests.
- The new `TRTLLMMetricsPayload` checks, exercised against synthetic `/metrics`
  documents: a healthy worker passes; zeroed gauges fail only the stats check;
  zeroed request counters fail only the request check; an attention-DP document
  with one idle rank passes. The shared base validators are untouched, so vLLM,
  SGLang and LMCache expectations do not move.
- `prek run` on the changed files: all hooks pass.
- `python3 docs/fern/scripts/docs_lint.py`: 0 errors.

Not run locally, needs the TRT-LLM container:

- `test_trtllm_unit.py` (skips at collection without CUDA).
  `test_init_llm_worker_engine_args_without_overrides` expects
  `enable_iter_perf_stats` false for `--publish-kv-events` alone and true for
  `--publish-metrics`, `--fpm-trace` or the port variable;
  `test_config_publish_forward_pass_metrics_opt_in` is new.
- `tests/serve/test_trtllm.py -k aggregated` (1 GPU), where the strengthened
  metric assertions run.

title: fix(runtime): ignored CLI certificate flags breaking frontend NATS TLS connections
body:
## Overview:

<!-- Describe your pull request here. Please read the text below the line, and make sure you follow the checklist.-->

On the frontend, NATS TLS CLI flags ( --nats-tls-ca-cert-path, --nats-tls-insecure) were silently ignored.

## Details:

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->

The cause was an ordering bug in main.py: 

```
	// line 355
	runtime = DistributedRuntime(...) // The Rust side reads those variables exactly once here
	....

	// line 411
   if config.nats_tls_ca_cert_path:
        os.environ["NATS_TLS_CA_CERT_PATH"] = config.nats_tls_ca_cert_path
    if config.nats_tls_insecure:
        os.environ["NATS_TLS_INSECURE"] = "1"
    else:
        # Clear any inherited NATS_TLS_INSECURE so --no-nats-tls-insecure can
        # override it before the Rust runtime reads the env var.
        os.environ.pop("NATS_TLS_INSECURE", None)

```

The Rust side reads those variables exactly once, during `DistributedRuntime` construction 

so by the time Python wrote them, nobody would ever read them again.

The identical "write env after runtime creation" pattern works fine for the TCP TLS flags right above it, because TCP reads its env vars lazily at each connection time. NATS reads eagerly at construction. 



Fix: 

pass both values as explicit `DistributedRuntime` constructor parameters instead of writing them back to the environment — no timing dependency at all.

Finally, both the environment variable and the CLI flag work for NATS TLS.

Option 1: environment variable

export NATS_TLS_CA_CERT_PATH=/etc/certs/ca.pem
dynamo.frontend --model-name my-model

Option 2: CLI flag

dynamo.frontend --model-name my-model --nats-tls-ca-cert-path /etc/certs/ca.pem

When both are set, the CLI flag wins

title: feat(sidecar): raw-vLLM NIXL P/D handoff adapter for standalone decode
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/15057/files) against `main`.

Implements the standalone decode sidecar's vLLM NIXL P/D handoff adapter (part of #13404). KV bytes never pass through the sidecar: the two vLLM workers transfer them directly, and this adapter only relays the connector metadata that tells the decode worker where to pull from.

## Path

```text
Gateway / EPP has already selected a prefill endpoint
    │
    │ POST /v1/chat/completions  +  x-prefiller-host-port
    ▼
standalone decode sidecar
    ├─ derived prefill-only request ──► selected raw-vLLM prefill worker
    │                            ◄──── kv_transfer_params
    ├─ validate handoff
    └─ original request + handoff ────► fixed local raw-vLLM decode worker
```

A request with valid P/D metadata no longer returns `pd_adapter_unavailable`. A request without the header keeps the existing decode passthrough byte for byte.

## Protocol pin

**vLLM v0.29.0**, revision string `vllm-v0.29.0-nixl-pull`, asserted at startup (`DYN_VLLM_NIXL_PROTOCOL_VERSION`); a mismatch refuses to start. `PROTOCOL.md` records the four sources reviewed at that tag, the field-by-field handoff contract with types and nullability, sanitized fixtures for all three messages, support status per request variant, the error taxonomy, and the upgrade checklist.

The handoff fields and flags were read from `NixlPullConnectorScheduler::request_finished` and `get_num_new_matched_tokens`, not inferred. `BlockIds` is `tuple[list[int], ...] | list[list[int]]` per `kv_connector/utils.py`.

## Design decisions worth reviewing

- **The decode destination is the locally configured engine.** `remote_host`/`remote_port` are connector side-channel information; they never become the HTTP target. C15 pins this.
- **A missing handoff is an error; an empty one is not.** A null or absent `kv_transfer_params` is `invalid_prefill_handoff` and the decode leg does not run. An empty `remote_block_ids` (`[]`, `[[]]`, `[[], []]`) is a *valid* handoff: it is what a full decode-side prefix-cache hit looks like, and the connector still needs the notification so the producer frees its blocks. C12 pins this.
- **Group nesting is preserved.** Flattening `remote_block_ids` would mis-address the KV cache groups. C11 pins this.
- **The whole validated object is forwarded, not a rebuilt subset.** Unknown connector fields, `tp_size`/`dcp_size`/`pp_size`, `remote_num_tokens`, `remote_blocks_expiry_time`, and `transfer_mode` all arrive verbatim. C13 pins this.
- **The connector's `remote_request_id` is never rewritten** to match the HTTP correlation id. C14 pins this.
- **Client-supplied `kv_transfer_params` is rejected** (non-empty): the adapter owns that field on this path. `null` and `{}` are tolerated as absent. C08 pins this.
- **`n != 1` is rejected before the prefill leg**, not silently rewritten to 1. C07 pins this.
- **Neither leg is retried.** A retry could duplicate generation or leak the producer's block lease; that needs its own idempotency design.

## Buffering and cancellation

Request bodies and prefill responses are both read under a hard cap, checked while reading rather than after (`413 pd_request_too_large`, `502 prefill_response_too_large`). The decode response stays a backpressured stream. Nothing buffers a whole generation.

Cancellation reuses the existing sidecar path: a second `CancellationToken` covers the prefill leg, and the decode leg keeps the existing `DecodeUpstream`/`Drop` semantics. Each cancellation case also asserts that the *next* leg was not dispatched.

## Adapter is opt-in

```bash
DYN_SIDECAR_PD_ADAPTER=vllm_nixl   # default: none
```

`none` keeps today's `UnavailablePdAdapter`, so a P/D request still fails explicitly with `501 pd_adapter_unavailable` until an operator opts in. Invalid values and an unimplemented protocol revision fail at startup, not on the first request. The no-header passthrough behaves identically in both modes.

## Tests

```
cargo test -p dynamo-epp-sidecar                        # 41 unit + 32 integration passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p dynamo-epp-sidecar --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt -p dynamo-epp-sidecar -- --check                        # clean
git diff --check                                                  # clean
```

All 32 integration tests run against ephemeral local fake workers — no GPU, no vLLM, no NIXL required. Each asserts both what the adapter sent and which legs it must *not* have called.

| ID | Case | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| C01 | no prefill header → passthrough | `c01_no_prefill_header_passes_through_to_decode` |
| C02 | non-streaming success; original params reach decode | `c02_*` (2 tests) |
| C03 | streaming success; no prefill token leaks | `c03_pd_streaming_success_keeps_decode_streaming` |
| C04 | `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` combinations | `c04_max_tokens_combinations` |
| C05 | `min_tokens`, `stream_options` prefill-only | `c05_min_tokens_and_stream_options_are_prefill_only` |
| C06 | unknown JSON / tools not lossily converted | `c06_unknown_fields_and_tools_survive_both_legs` |
| C07 | `n != 1` rejected, both legs uncalled | `c07_n_greater_than_one_is_rejected_before_any_leg` |
| C08 | injected handoff rejected; null/empty tolerated | `c08_client_injected_handoff_is_rejected_but_empty_is_tolerated` |
| C09 | missing / null / non-object handoff | `c09_missing_null_or_non_object_handoff_never_reaches_decode` |
| C10 | field missing / wrong type / bad port / wrong flags | `c10_field_level_handoff_errors_never_reach_decode` (10 sub-cases) |
| C11 | nested block groups preserved | `c11_nested_block_groups_are_preserved` |
| C12 | legally empty block groups accepted | `c12_legally_empty_block_groups_are_not_a_missing_handoff` |
| C13 | extra handoff fields forwarded intact | `c13_extra_handoff_fields_reach_decode_intact` |

| C16 | prefill 4xx/5xx: decode not run, status preserved, body not relayed | `c16_prefill_http_error_stops_before_decode` |
| C17 | non-JSON / truncated / SSE prefill | `c17_non_json_prefill_responses_stop_before_decode` |
| C18 | bounded request and response buffering | `c18_oversized_request_and_prefill_response_are_rejected_with_bounds` |
| C19 | prefill connect/read failures classified as prefill stage | `c19_prefill_connect_and_read_failures_are_prefill_stage_errors` |
| C20 | decode connect failure and status surfaced | `c20_decode_connect_error_and_status_are_not_swallowed` |
| C21 | decode bytes relayed verbatim, no fabricated `[DONE]` | `c21_decode_body_is_relayed_verbatim_without_a_fake_terminator` |
| C22 | cancel while prefill pending → no decode | `c22_cancellation_during_pending_prefill_prevents_decode` |
| C23 | cancel while handoff read parked → no decode | `c23_cancellation_after_partial_handoff_prevents_decode` |
| C24 | cancel / force shutdown while decode pending | `c24_*` (2 tests) |
| C25 | downstream drop ends the stream | `c25_downstream_drop_ends_a_pd_stream` |
| C26 | SSE bytes independent of upstream chunking | `c26_sse_chunk_boundaries_do_not_change_the_byte_stream` |
| C27 | 8 concurrent requests, shared client request id, no crossing | `c27_concurrent_requests_do_not_cross_handoffs` |
| C28 | IPv6 authority, query, base path | `c28_ipv6_endpoint_and_query_and_base_path_are_preserved` |
| C29 | hop-by-hop stripped, authorization/routing kept | `c29_hop_by_hop_headers_are_stripped_and_semantic_headers_kept` |
| C30 | disabled default, invalid config, protocol assertion | `c30_disabled_adapter_and_protocol_assertion` |

## Base

`402c2611ffcb3dbdeea344677d757dfed5469912`

## Not in this PR

- #13406 role-scoped catalogs and #13407 paired admission/reservation lifecycle.
- Worker discovery, fallback selection, and Kubernetes manifests.
- A generic multi-backend connector framework, and adapters for engines other than vLLM.
- Proxying KV bytes, or managing the producer's KV lease/heartbeat/GC.
- Cross-request or cross-session `kv_transfer_params` caching, and bidirectional KV caching.
- Full EPP P/D deployment validation and performance benchmarking.
- The EPP observability milestone. Optional sidecar stage/error tracing is deliberately not included; the observability plan reads the adapter's stage boundaries on its own branch after this merges.

## Known limitation: block lease ownership

The sidecar does not own the connector's block lease. A cancellation in the window between the handoff being produced and the decode worker accepting it relies on the producer's own lease expiry. HTTP cancellation here is **not** proof that GPU KV memory was released. `PROTOCOL.md` records this, and the smoke-test report will record what the pinned version actually does.

## Smoke test

A direct 1-prefill + 1-decode GPU smoke on two L20s with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0` (producer/consumer roles, KV load policy `fail`) is being run separately; results will be posted as a comment. It is **not** a full EPP/Kubernetes deployment acceptance and is not a performance claim.

title: fix(request-trace): emit pre-stream cancellations
body:
## Overview

Today, Dynamo can miss the final `request_end` trace when a client cancels a request before Dynamo sends the first response item. The request is counted as cancelled by the frontend, but its trace has no ending record.

This change writes the same existing `request_end` record for that cancellation path. It does not add a new event type or change the trace schema.

## What changes

- Keep the information needed for the final trace until the request finishes or is cancelled.
- If the engine marks the request as killed before the first response item, write one `request_end` record.
- Keep the current behavior for normal stream completion and cancellation after streaming begins.
- Prevent duplicate ending records if normal completion and cleanup both run.
- Leave other early errors unchanged.

A stream that is merely cleaned up is not enough to create a trace. The engine must have marked the request as killed.

## Validation

- All 70 focused request-trace tests passed.
- `cargo fmt` and `cargo check` passed.
- We deployed the patch on ARM64 under mirrored production traffic.
- During one complete hour, all 715 trace-eligible frontend completions had exactly one `request_end` trace: **715 / 715 (100%)**.
- All four cancelled requests in that hour had exactly one matching `request_end` trace.
- A direct cancellation before the first response produced `request_payload`, then `request_end` 456 ms later.
- An unpatched control during the same period had 816 traces for 817 eligible completions (99.88%).

title: feat(epp): observable request lifecycle, routing phases, and reservation callbacks
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/15056/files) against `main`.

Part of #11661 (Milestone 9 — Embedded EPP Observability). This is the first batch: request/phase instrumentation on the current EPP path. It does not close the milestone.

## What this adds

Extends the EPP's existing private Prometheus registry (`deploy/inference-gateway/ext-proc/src/metrics.rs`) with the request, phase, and lifecycle families. The exporter, the `/metrics` listener, the startup/discovery model-label binding, and `dynamo_epp_cached_tokens` are reused unchanged — no second registry, no second model labeling, no runtime initialization.

| Metric | Type | Labels | Observed at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dynamo_epp_requests_total` | counter | `model`, `outcome` | once per ext_proc attempt, at its terminal state |
| `dynamo_epp_request_duration_seconds` | histogram | `model`, `outcome` | same instant, measured from attempt start |
| `dynamo_epp_streams_inflight` | gauge | `model` | incremented when an attempt starts, decremented at its terminal state |
| `dynamo_epp_phase_duration_seconds` | histogram | `model`, `phase`, `outcome` | when a phase the attempt entered returns |
| `dynamo_epp_first_response_body_seconds` | histogram | `model` | on the first non-empty response body chunk |
| `dynamo_epp_lifecycle_callbacks_total` | counter | `model`, `operation`, `result` | when a picker lifecycle callback returns |
| `dynamo_epp_cached_tokens` | histogram | `model` | unchanged |

`outcome` ∈ {`response_eos`, `upstream_http_error`, `early_reject`, `ext_proc_error`, `incomplete`}; `phase` ∈ {`render_tokenize`, `selection`}; `operation` ∈ {`prefill_complete`, `request_complete`}; `result` ∈ {`ok`, `error`}. There is no `cancelled` result — a call site cannot reliably tell a cancelled call from a failed one, so it reports the failure rather than guessing.

The metric glossary lives in the module docs: exact observation points, what each family includes and does not include, the zero/absent/unknown rules, and the list of things that are not observable at this layer.

## Terminal classification

`result.is_ok()` is deliberately not consulted. The gRPC handler returns `Ok(())` both for a completed response and for an immediate rejection it already wrote, so the outcome is derived from the control flow, in a fixed priority order: early rejection → protocol error → upstream HTTP error status → completed response → incomplete.

- `incomplete` is what a disconnect or force shutdown actually is. It is not reported as a client cancellation, which this layer cannot distinguish.
- `upstream_http_error` uses the `:status` pseudo-header when the gateway forwards response headers, so a 5xx backend is not folded into `response_eos`.
- An attempt that never sees a response body records no `first_response_body_seconds` sample.
- Backend-reported `cached_tokens = 0` remains a real zero sample; a response with no usage information records nothing rather than a fabricated zero.

## Exactly-once terminal accounting

One `RequestObservation` owns one attempt. `finish()` is consuming, so an attempt records exactly one terminal; if the owning future is dropped first, `Drop` records `Incomplete` instead. A dropped stream therefore cannot leak the inflight gauge or disappear from the counters, and no shared request-keyed map is needed.

## Reservation lifecycle: calls, not state

`dynamo_epp_lifecycle_callbacks_total` counts callback invocations and their return. It is explicitly **not** an active-reservation gauge: `free_reservation` and `prefill_complete` are idempotent and return success for an unknown id without releasing anything, so `callback == Ok` must not decrement a state counter. Authoritative `Applied`/`NoChange` transitions need a core-level observer and are not claimed here.

## Structured events

`epp.request_finished` (finite `outcome`, `duration_ms`) and `epp.routing_failed` (`request_id`, finite `stage`, finite `code`, `reservation_taken`) carry bounded fields only. No prompt, token, authorization, raw handoff, worker address, or error message text is logged. These are tracing events on the existing subscriber; this PR does not add a JSON sink.

## Cardinality

`model` remains the startup/discovery-bound label; it is never read from a request body. Nothing request-scoped (request id, attempt id, reservation/plan/session id, prompt, cache salt, token, worker endpoint, peer IP, path/query/header) is a label. A test drives every label combination the schema allows and asserts the series count per family is exactly the enumeration product.

## Behavioural neutrality

Instrumentation does not change routing, status, headers, body, callback order, or cleanup semantics. The pre-existing wire-level integration test and all pre-existing unit tests pass unchanged.

## Tests

```
cargo test -p dynamo-ext-proc --lib          # 177 passed; 0 failed   (baseline 160; +17)
cargo test -p dynamo-ext-proc --test ext_proc_test   # 1 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p dynamo-ext-proc --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt -p dynamo-ext-proc -- --check                        # clean
git diff --check                                              # clean
```

New coverage:

- terminal taxonomy: `response_eos`, `upstream_http_error`, `early_reject`, `incomplete`; exactly-once terminal; inflight back to zero; body-free stream; two streams sharing a client request id;
- first body: recorded once, on the first *non-empty* chunk, never when no body arrives;
- recorder: `finish` + `Drop` records one terminal, not two; isolated registries do not share samples; exposition declares HELP/TYPE for every family;
- cardinality: every outcome, phase, operation, and result combination is driven once, and each family's series count equals its label product.

## Follow-up commits

- `b8974c7c48` condenses the module documentation into one glossary plus the readings most likely to be
  misread, and drops two tests that asserted properties the compiler or the test helper already
  guarantees. No runtime path changed; `175` lib tests pass.

## Base

`402c2611ffcb3dbdeea344677d757dfed5469912`

## Not in this PR

- Authoritative reservation transitions and scheduler load snapshots (needs a reviewed core observer; `HostTelemetry` is a candidate, its snapshot granularity needs checking first).
- Replica connection/sync-lag signals. The discovery set does not prove a peer registered or caught up, so no such series is published; `discovered` / `register` / `deregister` operation outcomes follow separately.
- Sidecar and paired P/D stages, which wait on #13404 and #13406/#13407 respectively.
- Real TTFT/ITL and per-token progress: no token-boundary signal exists at this layer.
- Output-growth accounting and worker filtering.
- A JSON log sink (the current fmt subscriber does not imply one).

## Notes for review

- `ExtProcServer::new` now takes the recorder instead of reaching a global, which is what lets the tests assert on an isolated registry. `EppRouter::from_selector` takes it for the same reason.
- The `:status` capture only fires when the gateway forwards response headers; when it is absent the attempt is classified without it, and the glossary says so.
- `selection` includes queue wait and `render_tokenize` includes renderer latency. They are named for the phase, not for compute, on purpose.


Test and benchmark sources are retained locally; the validation results below refer to those local files.

title: fix(vllm): report pause state with weight version
body:
## Summary

Add live `paused` state to the Python vLLM worker's `get_weight_version` response, queried under `_pause_lock`. Controllers can distinguish a serving worker from one left paused after a weight update. A downstream replay failure left a paused worker receiving traffic and hanging requests, motivating this observation.

Pause query succeeds (`true` means paused; `false` means unpaused):

```json
{"status": "ok", "version": "checkpoint-1", "paused": false}
```

Pause query fails or returns an invalid value:

```json
{"status": "ok", "version": "checkpoint-1", "paused": null}
```

Failures are logged; version retrieval still succeeds. `null` means unknown, not unpaused. No error-detail field is added. `EngineDeadError` retains the existing shutdown behavior. The original `getattr(self, "_weight_version", "initial")` is preserved, including its missing-attribute fallback.

`paused` is unconditional so callers use one response shape; clients with closed schemas must accept the added boolean-or-null field. The query still waits for the engine and lock, and follows vLLM's pause semantics, without an all-DP-rank guarantee. Readiness and routing are unchanged.

title: fix(frontend): Flush buffered byte-fallback decoding
body:
## Overview:

Prevent frontend response failures caused by incremental byte-fallback decoding while preserving the tokenizer’s full-decode output.

A later malformed byte can cause Hugging Face’s ByteFallback decoder to reinterpret an entire byte-token run, including a prefix Dynamo has already emitted. The companion tokenizer change buffers that unstable suffix. This PR integrates terminal flushing into Dynamo so buffered text is not lost when generation ends.

## Details:

- Consume the companion tokenizer fix, which buffers unfinished byte-fallback runs while retaining the append-only guard for other unexpected rewrites.
- Flush buffered text at EOS, terminal chunks, bare end-of-stream, and engine-decoded terminal responses.
- Preserve stop-sequence buffering, output ordering, error propagation, and per-token metadata.
- Add self-contained Rust regression coverage for byte-fallback boundaries and terminal/stop handling. The tests require no running frontend, model weights, GPUs, or Kubernetes.
- Pin the companion tokenizer commit in both the root and Python-binding Cargo workspaces so direct and transitive consumers resolve the same patched implementation.

Companion tokenizer change:
https://github.com/ai-dynamo/frontend-crates/compare/main...alexeldeib:ace/stable-byte-fallback-decode

The tokenizer fix should be published first; I'll replace both temporary review pins with the published release before publishing this PR.

Then review the companion tokenizer change in `tokenizers/src/lib.rs` and `tokenizers/src/hf.rs`. Finally, check `Cargo.toml` and `lib/bindings/python/Cargo.toml` to confirm both workspaces resolve the same patched tokenizer source.

title: feat(epp): add role-scoped worker catalogs for standalone disaggregated routing
body:
## Summary

Closes #13406 (DEP #11661, Milestone 5). With
`DYN_EPP_TOPOLOGY_MODE=disaggregated`, the standalone Rust EPP splits the pods selected by one
`InferencePool` into prefill and decode catalogs using a configurable worker-role label, and drives
two independent embedded `SelectionService` instances from them.

**Two instances, not one instance with two routing groups.** `use_kv_events` is fixed when a
`SelectionService` is built and differs per role, and the two catalogs must be disjoint so a decode
pick can never see a prefill worker. Everything else that separates the roles is *per-request*: the
decode selector carries the same `RouterConfigOverride` the Dynamo-runtime EPP applies to its decode
leg (`decode_router_config_override`, shared from `epp.rs`) and supplies it on every selection and
booking; prefill and aggregated carry none.

| | prefill | decode |
|---|---|---|
| static `use_kv_events` | base | `false` |
| static `router_predicted_ttl_secs` | base | cleared (needs events) |
| per-request `RouterConfigOverride` | none | `overlap_score_credit: 0.0`, `assume_kv_reuse: false`, `track_prefill_tokens: false` |

Prefill scores prefix overlap and does not model long-lived block occupancy; decode ignores overlap
and does model occupancy. A decode worker did not compute the prompt, so charging it prefill work
would mis-rank it, and crediting it for a prefix it never cached would be a fiction. Decode workers
therefore carry no `kv_events_endpoint` and no `replay_endpoint`, which is exactly what makes them
Schedulable under `use_kv_events=false`.

**Prefill is a selection input only.** All five reflector reads on the request path are scoped to the
serving role, and an empty decode catalog returns the new `PickError::RoleCatalogEmpty` (503)
instead of falling back to a prefill endpoint. `build_request_header_response` is the sole producer
of `x-gateway-destination-endpoint` and is reachable only through `pick()`, so scoping `pick()`
scopes the whole surface.

**Aggregated mode is unchanged.** The role label is never read, one catalog is built, and the
existing single-selector path runs byte-identically.

### Requirement-by-requirement

| # | Issue requirement | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Topology configuration + worker-role label contract | `epp_standalone_config.rs` — `EppTopologyMode`, `DYN_EPP_WORKER_ROLE_LABEL` (default `nvidia.com/dynamo-worker-role`), label-key syntax validation |
| 2 | Split eligible pool pods into prefill/decode sets | `pod_discovery.rs` — `raw_worker_from_pod` resolves the role after the existing eligibility gates |
| 3 | Role-scoped catalogs, KV-event inputs, readiness, selector config | `pod_discovery.rs` (`IndexState`/`RoleCounts`), `role_config.rs`, `selector.rs`, `topology_adapter.rs` |
| 4 | Prefill never selected as a destination | `epp_router.rs` `serving_role`, `picker.rs` `RoleCatalogEmpty`, `server.rs` 503 mapping |
| 5 | Unit + integration coverage | 18 net new test functions over `main` (table-style; 161 in the crate) across role changes, missing/invalid labels, add/remove reconciliation, and the routing invariant |

### New environment variables

`DYN_EPP_TOPOLOGY_MODE`, `DYN_EPP_WORKER_ROLE_LABEL`, and two per-role capacity overrides
(`DYN_EPP_{PREFILL,DECODE}_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS`) that fall back to the shared value. Real P/D
fleets differ by 8–16× here, and `max_num_batched_tokens` is the denominator of
`PolicyClassConfig::worker_is_busy`. Per-role KV-block totals are deliberately not added: nothing in
this split consumes distinct totals yet.

Two configurations are rejected at startup rather than silently reinterpreted: `DYN_EPP_PEER_SERVICE`
with `disaggregated` (both instances would bind the one hardcoded `replica-agg` port; Milestone 8 /

title: fix(sglang): pass the prefill dp rank to sglang decode
body:
## Overview:

In SGLang disaggregated serving with a data-parallel prefill, the decode engine has to know which prefill DP rank owns a request's KV before it can create its KV receiver. SGLang's own router sends that rank in the decode request (`disagg_prefill_dp_rank`). Dynamo chooses the rank in the frontend but never forwarded it to the decode leg, so SGLang's decode fell back to resolving the rank over HTTP against the prefill's bootstrap server. The prefill cannot start its forward until the decode receiver has registered, so that round trip is serial in front of every prefill.

Measured with SGLang's per-request time statistics (`--enable-request-time-stats-logging`) on a GLM-5.2 PD deployment with a 4-way DP prefill, per request:

| | without this change | with this change |
|---|---|---|
| decode `bootstrap_duration` | 150 ms to 650 ms depending on load (p90 up to 1.1 s) | 0.3 ms to 0.6 ms |
| prefill `bootstrap_duration` | 170 ms to 860 ms | 0.4 ms to 53 ms |
| requests parked in the decode pre-allocation queue | 3.7 to 6.8 per DP rank | 0 |
| client TTFT minus prefill `forward_duration` | 0.22 s to 0.64 s | 0.04 s to 0.06 s |

The native SGLang router reads 0.25 ms on the same decode metric.

## Details:

- `lib/llm/src/kv_router/prefill_router/mod.rs`: `PrefillOutcome::Bootstrap` and `PreparedPrefill` carry the prefill DP rank the router selected, and `into_decode_request` writes it to the decode leg's `routing.prefill_dp_rank`. The prefill leg already had it (`prepare_prefill_dispatch`); the decode leg is a clone taken before dispatch and only received `prefill_worker_id`.
- `components/src/dynamo/sglang/_compat.py`: `prefill_dp_rank_kwargs` builds `{"disagg_prefill_dp_rank": rank}` filtered through `filter_supported_async_generate_kwargs`, so an SGLang release without the argument receives nothing.
- `components/src/dynamo/sglang/request_handlers/llm/decode_handler.py`: passes it on the disaggregated `async_generate` call and on the native-payload builder.
- `components/src/dynamo/sglang/engine_generate.py`: `build_native_generate_request` accepts `prefill_dp_rank` and sets `disagg_prefill_dp_rank` when the installed `GenerateReqInput` has the field.
- Tests: the Rust decode-leg test asserts the rank is carried; Python tests cover the helper against engines with and without the argument, the disaggregated decode path forwarding the rank, and the native builder.

Every existing reader of `routing.prefill_dp_rank` is phase-gated (KV selector pinned-worker hint, session-affinity explicit target, SGLang and vLLM sidecar converters) and uses `dp_rank` alone for Decode and Aggregated, so setting the field on the decode leg does not change decode routing. The bootstrap room already encoded the rank (`compute_bootstrap_room`), but SGLang only trusts that encoding when the prefill runs `--load-balance-method follow_bootstrap_room`; sending the rank explicitly works for every load-balance method.

Not covered here: the multimodal decode handler (its request model has no routing block) and the Rust SGLang sidecar's decode request builder, which has the same gap and can now read the rank from the decode leg. Both are follow-ups.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`into_decode_request` in `lib/llm/src/kv_router/prefill_router/mod.rs`, then `_compat.prefill_dp_rank_kwargs` and its two call sites in `decode_handler.py`.

## Related Issues

**🚫 This PR is NOT linked to an issue**:
- [x] Confirmed — no related issue

## Validation

- `cargo check -p dynamo-llm --tests`, `cargo fmt --check`, and the 17 `kv_router::prefill_router::tests` pass (including the extended decode-leg test).
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes (isort, black, flake8, ruff, codespell).
- New Python tests compile; they need an SGLang install and run in CI.
- Verified end to end against SGLang's request time statistics: with the change the decode `bootstrap_duration` drops to sub-millisecond and the decode pre-allocation queue empties (table above).

title: refactor(replay): delegate Weka ingestion to AISimulate
body:
#### Summary

Replace Dynamo's duplicate Weka parser and converter with AISimulate's graph loader. Keep `trace_format="weka"` as a compatibility adapter and execute the resulting graph through the existing typed agentic replay path.

- Remove the Dynamo Weka parser, lowering code, converter binary, and their build targets.
- Preserve source block sizes, explicit nested timestamp overrides, and the resolved timestamp basis in offline/online summaries and runner metadata.
- Retain source-model provenance and the configured execution target; adapt to the required AISimulate API changes.
- Keep the router implementation unchanged apart from the new protocol field required by AISimulate.

#### Weka behavior changes

- `auto` selects one nested timestamp basis for the whole corpus. Adding a relative-timestamp witness can change other files' interpretation. The resolved basis is reported; explicit `absolute` retains before-marker rejection.
- `out: 0` remains zero, replacing the former `max(1, out)` normalization; output totals and timing/throughput metrics can change.
- Missing/null `api_time` remains absent in provenance; dependency classification uses a zero-duration interval instead of rejecting the input.

These differences are documented in the CLI reference.

#### AISimulate nightly migration

Pin Python/benchmarks/containers to `aisimulate==0.13.0.dev202609230000000054` and both Cargo manifests plus all three lockfiles to `aisimulate-core = "=0.13.0-dev.202609230000000054"`. Both are published; NVIDIA wheel staging also lists this release. No Git source overrides are required.

This release removes the old AIC import namespaces. Update planner, profiler, runtime helpers, tests and collection stubs to `aisimulate` / `aisimulate_core`, including `aisimulate.capacity` and `aisimulate.legacy_cli`. Adapt planner construction to the canonical forward-pass configuration API while preserving regression-only operation and native-to-regression fallback.

Lower resolved canonical op-level timing through Dynamo's existing AIC callback, retaining materialized KV capacity. Reject unsupported non-default timing controls explicitly. Initialize the new synthetic cached-prefix field to zero. The nightly now samples vLLM's first token at prefill completion, so both vLLM and SGLang parity checks compare TTFT to context latency without an extra decode step; the 5% tolerance is unchanged. The decode-worker midpass test now uses decode latency to establish its in-flight boundary.

#### Prediction changes beyond Weka

The dependency upgrade also changes AIC and replay predictions for non-Weka workloads. In the reviewer's comparison of `0.12.0` with the previous September 17 nightly, Qwen/Qwen3-32B on h200_sxm showed roughly 1.69 ms higher AIC TPOT (8.0–9.2% across measured ISLs), unchanged context latency, and SGLang TTFT without the extra decode step. These are historical measurements of that earlier nightly, not measurements of the current September 23 pin or a guarantee for other models/systems. The current nightly also emits vLLM's first token at prefill completion; both backend parity oracles now reflect that behavior. Prediction baselines may therefore change outside Weka as well.

#### Validation

The local results below were collected during the upgrade through `8a5fbade09`; they do not validate the subsequent main merge `ab14ca4a84`.

- Built the native runtime with `aic-forward-pass` against the published 0.13 nightly, in a fresh Python 3.12 environment with no `aiconfigurator` or `aiconfigurator_core` packages.
- Main upgrade suite: **1,581 passed, 8 existing unsupported-combination skips**, covering planner/profiler unit tests, native AIC/task integration, replay/binding and dependency checks. Supplementary simulation checks: **31 passed**, including rejection of unsupported timing controls.
- Unified CLI: **19 passed**. Canonical AIC execution includes both vLLM and SGLang with fixed and automatically estimated capacity; all **8 integration cases passed after the final capacity change** (`8a5fbade09`).
- Rust mocker: **216 passed**. Mocker CI-style Clippy, Python binding Clippy with `aic-forward-pass`, formatting and pre-commit passed.
- Ordinary wheel installs on Python 3.11/3.13 plus native Weka checks: **12 passed each**. Wheel AIC import/data/performance-model smoke passed. Matching locally built Dynamo runtime wheels were supplied via `--find-links`.
- Hosted CI for the current head is pending. Full container builds, GPU lanes, aarch64 and macOS execution were not run locally. The wheel remains Linux-only.

[AISimulate #234](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aisimulate/pull/234) remains open and its future-parent regression is absent from this nightly; the P3 dependency thread stays open. The previous requirement to wait for a release retaining legacy AIC imports is superseded by this migration.

title: fix(frontend): reject continuation across reordered messages
body:
## Overview:

Reject `continue_final_message` when the prompt formatter moves the final input message ahead of other messages. Without this check, continuation can truncate the rendered prompt and discard later tool results.

## Details:

- Use the selected formatter’s media order to detect the incompatible request and return `InvalidArgument` before tokenization.
- Preserve continuation for ordered tool results and assistant prefixes.
- Add a regression covering reordered tool results, valid continuation cases, and requests with continuation disabled.
- Validated with focused unit tests and dev HTTP checks, including streaming and non-streaming rejection. The final rebase preserves the tested Rust code and dependencies.

## Where should the reviewer start?

title: chore: OPS-8654 bump trtllm to v1.3.0rc27
body:
Linear: OPS-8654

## Overview:

Automated dependency upgrade to TensorRT-LLM `1.3.0rc27`, plus the changes the upgrade turned out to need: a fix in the dpkg license generator, a correction to the DALI block and its note, an ignore list for new deprecation warnings, and a per-architecture Open MPI selection with its settings and login-profile fixes, a hostname workaround so Open MPI 5 can start workers on arm64, and tests that guard the MPI setup.

## Details:

### The upgrade (`72028898`, `a3bda421`)

`container/context.yaml` runtime tag, the `pyproject.toml` pin, both per-arch baseline SBOMs re-captured against `1.3.0rc27`, the DALI pin moved from 2.1.1 to 2.2.0 to match the base image, and the release and compatibility pages. The manifest also closes a gap on `main`, where the baseline SBOM recorded `1.3.0rc25` while `container/context.yaml` recorded `1.3.0rc26`.

### The licenses stage (`a95a2263`, `c4e8e573`, `a9c56d28`)

`trtllm-runtime` and `trtllm-runtime-efa` both stopped at:

```
[dpkg] dpdk-community@26.03.0.5-1: license is UNKNOWN and policy.licenses.unknown = 'deny' (SPDX: 'UNKNOWN')
```

The rc27 base image installs `dpdk-community` and `doca-sdk-common` while it is built, and removes them again without purging them. dpkg keeps both entries in the `config-files` state: it deleted the packages' files and kept their conffiles, and those still ship. `doca-sdk-common` leaves `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/doca-runtime-<arch>-linux-gnu.conf` and `/etc/profile.d/doca-runtime.sh`, and `dpdk-community` leaves `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/dpdk-<arch>-linux-gnu.conf`. syft, which captures the baseline SBOMs, catalogs installed packages only, so both entries survive baseline subtraction and reach the policy gate. rc25 and rc26 carried the same pair as `doca-sdk-common` and `mlnx-dpdk`, and both have a `license_overrides.yaml` entry, which is why the gate passed until upstream renamed the DPDK package.

`dpdk-community` has no license the generator can read: the package ships no copyright file at all. The `dpdk-community_26.03.0.5-1_amd64.deb` from the public DOCA 3.5.0 repository has none, and its only SPDX tags are seven `BSD-3-Clause` tags. `a9c56d28` adds a `BSD-3-Clause` override, like the existing `mlnx-dpdk` entry.

The generator now reads each entry's dpkg state (`${db:Status-Status}`). It skips a `config-files` entry only when dpkg lists its conffiles and none of them is on disk, and it logs every kept entry with its surviving conffiles. An earlier version on this branch (`a95a2263`) skipped every `config-files` entry. Review showed that their conffiles ship, so `a9c56d28` narrowed the skip.

### The DALI block (`eed14723`)

rc27 ships DALI 2.2.0 in the base image, so the pinned install is a no-op and three statements in the note above the block described the old base. The note is corrected, and one hole in the code is closed: the decoder enumeration finds its library with `find ... -name 'libavcodec*.so*'` and loops over the result, so an empty match checked nothing and exited 0. A release that links the codec into a differently named library, which is what PyNvVideoCodec 2.2.0 does three blocks below, passed that guard while shipping decoders. Both the `runtime_full` block and the post-overlay guard now fail on an empty match.

### The codec waiver (`24344f20`)

Text only. The DALI waiver in `container/compliance/policy/codec_policy.yaml` ends with "Re-measure when the vendored version moves." It moved, so the rc27 measurement is recorded there. Two statements in the same note needed the same pass: it said the Dockerfile pins `nvidia-dali-cuda130>=2.1.1`, where the pin is exact and now reads `==2.2.0`, and it said one guard runs "after the upgrade", where that install is a no-op.

### The rc27 deprecations (`04cdba0b`)

Three trtllm tests failed at import time, not on an assertion: `cutlass.utils.LayoutEnum is deprecated`. The rc27 base ships nvidia-cutlass-dsl `4.8.0.dev0` where rc26 shipped `4.6.2`, and it moves names out of `cutlass.utils` and `cutlass.arch` behind a module `__getattr__` that warns. flashinfer is `0.6.18` in both images and still reads the old locations, some in class-body annotations that run at import time, as does TensorRT-LLM's own `cute_dsl_kernels`. Under `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]` the import raises. Two ignore entries cover all four warnings the import gains between the two images.

### The fourth glob loop (`f502244d`)

This file has four loops that enumerate a vendored FFmpeg library. The DALI commit above closed three. This closes the post-overlay PyNvVideoCodec one, with the counter its own sibling in `runtime_full` already uses.

### The MPI path (`1ff5387a`, `f04ff8d1`, `69d62c63`, `2111e3f2`, `fc14cb34`, `7b05507e`)

rc27 repointed `/opt/hpcx/ompi` and `/usr/local/mpi` from `ompi4` to `ompi5`, so the image defaults to Open MPI `5.0.10rc2` where rc26 defaulted to `4.1.9a1`. TensorRT-LLM spawns its executor ranks with `MPI.COMM_SELF.Spawn`. On amd64 that spawn fails on `ompi5` with `ucp_ep_create(proc=0) failed: Destination is unreachable`, the worker never binds its gRPC port, and the serving tests wait out their deadlines. On arm64 `ompi4` is not an option: the base image's `libtorch_cpu.so` needs `ompi_mpi_short_float`, which only `ompi5` defines.

`1ff5387a` links `/opt/dynamo/mpi` to `ompi4` on amd64 and to `ompi5` on arm64. The `PATH`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `OPAL_PREFIX` entries name that link, in `runtime_full` and in `pre_runtime`, which the shipped image builds on. Transitional: delete the link and the entries when upstream's `ompi5` can spawn.

`f04ff8d1` completes the switch to `ompi4`. The base image edits `etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf` only in the Open MPI it selects itself, so `ompi4` kept `hwloc_base_binding_policy = core` and `btl = self`. With `core`, `import tensorrt_llm` pins the process and every child to CPUs 0-1. With `btl = self`, `mpirun --mca pml ob1`, which the operator's multi-node launch uses, cannot connect two ranks. The commit applies the base image's two edits to the selected MPI and fails the build if either setting survives.

`69d62c63` makes the dev images' login profile, `container/dev/50-framework-paths.sh`, prefer `/opt/dynamo/mpi`. It used to reset login shells, SSH sessions and later dev-image RUN steps to `/opt/hpcx/ompi`, which is ompi5 in rc27.

`2111e3f2` replaces the affinity test with `tests/dependencies/test_trtllm_mpi.py`, which checks the whole selection in the built image: the link's target per architecture, the library mpi4py loads, a `MPI.COMM_SELF.Spawn`, a two-rank `ob1` launch, and the CPU affinity.

`fc14cb34` fixes what that spawn check found on arm64. Open MPI 5 cannot spawn from a singleton when the hostname length plus the digits of its pid exceeds 37, and TRT-LLM starts its workers that way. CI's pod names are 46 (arm64) and 50 (amd64) characters long. amd64 avoids the defect by running ompi4, which is likely the real reason the serving tests failed on ompi5 there. arm64 cannot, so where the image selects ompi5, a `.pth` line imports `_dynamo_pmix_hostname` when Python starts. It sets `PMIX_HOSTNAME` to a short name only in processes that no MPI launcher started, on hosts whose names are longer than 30 characters. Ranks that mpirun or prte start get `PMIX_HOSTNAME` from the launcher and keep the real hostname. A real multi-node launch is not verified: a Python process that runs a multi-node `mpirun` itself would pass the short name on to it. The operator's multi-node launch starts `mpirun` from `/bin/sh`, so the hook does not run there.

The cause is in Open MPI itself: it passes the singleton's name to `prte` through a 50-byte print buffer, so a long name is cut short and `prte` registers the wrong one. It is fixed upstream in open-mpi/ompi#14398 (v5.0.x backport: open-mpi/ompi#14409), and Mellanox/ompi's `v5.0.x_hpcx` branch has had the fix since Mellanox/ompi#61. No release has it yet: Open MPI 5.0.11 does not, and TRT-LLM 1.3.0rc28 still ships HPC-X v2.50 with Open MPI 5.0.10rc2 and fails the same spawn. `7b05507e` records when to remove each part of the workaround. Delete the hook once a base image's HPC-X passes a spawn with a 46-character hostname without it. Delete the amd64 Open MPI 4 selection only when Open MPI 5 also spawns on amd64 without the hook, in CI and on a host with extra network interfaces. Tracked in NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#19607.

### The CUDA IPC test (`7a57fd6a`, `d8b48f54`)

`7a57fd6a` passes the consumer's result through the queue as a numpy array, reports child errors, and always cleans up its processes. It also built the expected tensor with a CPU float16 `arange`. Past 2048 that rounds differently from the producer's CUDA `arange`, so the assertion failed whenever the transfer worked. `d8b48f54` builds `expected` on the GPU again.

### The LD_PRELOAD order (`d4bfa7d9`)

The ENV block named `/opt/dynamo/libstdc++.so.6` in `LD_PRELOAD` before the RUN that creates it. Every command in between printed `ERROR: ld.so: object '/opt/dynamo/libstdc++.so.6' from LD_PRELOAD cannot be preloaded`. The RUN now comes first.

### The merge of main

main cut v1.5.0, which rewrote the three release tables this branch touches. `docs/fern/components/releases.data.ts` is the source of truth and merged cleanly with both sides. The two conflicted pages are generated from it, so they were taken from main and regenerated rather than hand-resolved, and `gen_llms_tables.py --check` reports every marker-spliced page unchanged.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`container/compliance/generators/dpkg.py`, and the new `container/compliance/tests/test_dpkg_generator.py` beside it. Then `container/templates/trtllm_runtime.Dockerfile` around `/opt/dynamo/mpi`, for the MPI selection and its settings edit. The rest of the diff is the version bump and comments.

## Validation

| Claim | How verified | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| The gate fails on `dpdk-community`, and stops failing | CI job `105736243907` before, CI build job `107383547938` at `fc14cb34` after, step `licenses` on both architecture legs | `License validation failed: 1 violation(s) across 1063 packages` | `License validation passed: 1064 packages, no violations` on `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, each naming the two kept packages and their conffiles |
| The removed packages still ship files | `dpkg-query -W -f='${Conffiles}'` and `ls` in the rc27 base image and in the built image | state `config-files` for `dpdk-community` and `doca-sdk-common` | the same three conffiles on disk in both images; `doca-runtime.sh` and one `ld.so.conf.d` file carry an NVIDIA proprietary header |
| The override is what makes the gate pass | The `licenses` stage's generator and policy commands, in the CI test image for `1ff5387a`, amd64, baseline `release@2af29022` | without the new override: 528 collected, 27 left, `License validation failed: 1 violation(s)`, `dpdk-community` UNKNOWN | with it: 528 collected, 0 skipped, 27 left, `License validation passed` |
| Other images do not move | `dpkg-query` on built `sglang-runtime` and `vllm-runtime` images | no entry outside `installed` | unchanged |

build: compile NVTX ranges into runtime wheels via the header-only nvtx crate
body:
## Summary

Make the runtime's NVTX ranges shippable.

### Compile NVTX ranges into runtime wheels

The Rust runtime annotates the frontend hot path (`preprocess.*`, `route.*`, `transport.*`, `detokenize`) behind the `nvtx` Cargo feature and the `DYN_ENABLE_RUST_NVTX` runtime gate. The feature was absent from the wheel builds, so in every published wheel the macros expand to nothing and the runtime gate has no effect. It could not simply be enabled: the ranges went through `cudarc::nvtx`, whose build links `libnvToolsExt.so`, the NVTX v2 shared library that CUDA 12.9 removed. The CUDA 13 base images ship only the `nvtx3/*.h` headers, so a wheel built with the feature either fails to link or fails to import.

- `lib/runtime/src/nvtx.rs` now delegates to the `nvtx` crate, which compiles the header-only NVTX v3 shim into the binary. No shared library at build or run time; Nsight attaches through its injection library at launch as before. The macros and the `DYN_ENABLE_RUST_NVTX` gate are unchanged. The crate is already a workspace dependency through kvbm.
- `nvtx` is added to the maturin feature lists in the wheel builder. With the feature compiled in and the gate unset, each range site costs one relaxed atomic load.
- `dynamo.common.utils.nvtx_utils` degrades to its existing no-op path with a warning when `DYN_NVTX=1` is set but the `nvtx` Python package is absent, instead of failing at import. Profiling presets set that variable on every launch, and not every serving image ships the package.

## Validation

- `cargo check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` on `dynamo-runtime` with and without the `nvtx` feature; `cargo check -p dynamo-llm --features nvtx`; `cargo fmt --check`.
- A runtime wheel built with the feature on a CUDA 13 aarch64 SGLang image: `ldd` on `_core.abi3.so` shows no `libnvToolsExt` dependency, the NVTX symbols are present, `from dynamo.runtime import DistributedRuntime` and the `dynamo.frontend` and `dynamo.sglang` entry points work.
- Serving with that wheel under `DYN_ENABLE_RUST_NVTX=1`: the frontend and workers log "NVTX annotations enabled", and the frontend's Nsight report contains the `preprocess.*`, `route.*`, `transport.*`, and `detokenize` ranges.
- `nvtx_utils` import guard checked by importing the module with the package made unavailable.
- `pre-commit` passes on every changed file.

## Known limitations

- The CI multi-arch wheel builds are the remaining check for the x86 and CUDA 12 variants.
