title: feat(replay): add conversation affinity to the existing adapter
body:
## Summary

Extend Dynamo’s existing `ai-dynamo` replay runner, `dynamo.router` provider and native `KvReplayComposition` so AISimulate users can configure KV-aware placement with independent conversation affinity:

```yaml
router:
  policy: kv_router
  affinity:
    mode: sibling_group  # or session
    ttl_seconds: 3600
```

The existing `aisimulate predict --config agentx.yaml` entry point executes the native policy and reports actual worker/attention-DP placement and physical cache reuse. No new Python distribution or alternate policy implementation is introduced. AISimulate remains the engine/round-robin package; installing existing `ai-dynamo` supplies routing through its existing entry points. This follows [the installation-boundary review in AISimulate #306](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aisimulate/pull/306#discussion_r4087684968).

- Reuse current-main `DefaultWorkerSelector` from `dynamo-custom-policy-builtin`, `PolicyQueue`, `SessionAffinity`, the existing replay indexer and physical KV-event bridge. Add group-key mapping, simulated time and Hold/Lease ownership around accepted dispatch; the selector, affinity table and eviction algorithms remain native.
- Reuse AISimulate’s existing Python runner and shared serialized executor for snapshots, warmup, duration, timing and reports, passing the existing Dynamo composition. Supported conversation/profile paths are static offline vLLM/SGLang aggregated and P/D with attention DP. Reject incompatible Planner/backend/config combinations explicitly. Retain legacy explicit runner and replay paths.
- Pin actual AISimulate source **60fd1bb74a78339e7090161866c5e93d299dc65f**, exact version 0.13.0, in both Rust manifests and three existing lockfiles. Python/container dependencies use the same version; the container builds the existing AISimulate wheel from that immutable source. Strict runtime version/API and dependency checks remain; no local override or new lockfile is used.
- Update existing AISimulate 0.12 Python import paths to 0.13 namespaces across Replay, Planner, Profiler and native timing helpers, including their existing test/marker configuration. These are required by the package-wide dependency upgrade, not additional integration layers.
- Correct an existing mid-pass test fixture that deadlocked on a zero-duration decode pass. The failure reproduces on unmodified Dynamo/core 0.12; the fixture now establishes an actual 100ms decode window without changing production timing or scheduler behavior.

## Dependency and installation boundary

This draft targets current Dynamo main, using interfaces already merged there. **Dynamo #15149 is not required and remains independent.** Source dependency is one-way: this Dynamo consumer depends on the neutral hooks from AISimulate #306 (stacked on #307). AISimulate’s core/wheel does not depend on Dynamo. Merge/publish the matching AISimulate source before finalizing the downstream release dependency; do not confuse a buildable source pair with a published package.

Only the existing `aisimulate`, `ai-dynamo` and `ai-dynamo-runtime` packages are used. The [AISimulate quickstart](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aisimulate/blob/harrli/aic-1817-routing/docs/agentx-quickstart.md) records source-build prerequisites and complete YAML; its Dynamo revision is pinned to the tested source build. No GPU or running Dynamo service is required for offline replay.

## Validation

- Clean source-paired installation uses existing wheels only: AISimulate **60fd1bb7** and Dynamo **44253532ec**. All three matching wheels were rebuilt from clean commits and installed normally; all 156 dependencies and key installed-module source hashes agree. Native core/API version checks and `pip check` pass, with imports from installed site-packages and no source/native overrides.
- Mocker library: **223/223 passed**; all-target Clippy passes with warnings denied. Native coverage includes accepted-dispatch affinity commit, abort, fractional virtual TTL, queue progress, snapshot identity, and actual aggregated/P-D DP/cache behavior.
- Installed CLI checks cover the existing round-robin/KV/Planner entry points plus YAML-selected conversation routing across vLLM/SGLang, aggregated/P-D, session/sibling affinity, warmup/duration, cache-off controls and resource refusal. **38 passed** (including real default-AIC and resolved-op-level Sweeper execution); Replay/Router unit tests **64 passed**.
- Planner’s real native estimator and online-regression tests: **35 passed**, including dense TP1/TP2 and all three backend identities. The 0.13 canonical constructor replaces removed constructors. Unknown Mocker backend identity requires an explicit AIC performance-model backend; it is not relabeled as vLLM.
- Static-vs-replay parity: **12 passed**. The SGLang first-token expectation now follows its already-merged prefill behavior; the 5% tolerance, TPOT and throughput checks are unchanged.
- The complete documented AIC-timed P/D quickstart passes for **3,600 seconds** (219 completed requests, 95.6497% actual prefix reuse) and **600 seconds** (42 completed, 96.1709%). Both have zero cancellations/unsettled server requests. Native decisions match actual worker/DP placement; counts are observations, not deterministic golden values.
- Strict dependency checks: **5 passed**. Three locked/offline metadata graphs resolve the same immutable core without a core-to-Dynamo cycle. Eight container contexts render; existing wheel-install smoke tests use the actual source-paired AISimulate artifact.
- AISimulate-only wheel: default engine succeeds; configured Dynamo routing exits 2 with the integration named explicitly.

This remains a draft pending current remote CI and required human review. The earlier container installation failure was an unpublished 0.13 package lookup; the runtime/frontend installers now consume their staged matching source wheel. A local wheel smoke is not a claim that all remote container tests have passed.

Functional simulation does not establish measured GPU accuracy or full live AgentX recipe parity. Required CI, CODEOWNER/domain review and merge permissions remain separate gates.

Related: [AIC-1817](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/AIC-1817), [AIC-1813](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/AIC-1813), ai-dynamo/aisimulate#306, ai-dynamo/aisimulate#307.

Pin `da848eb78eec6331d670b8d80b5b0b8333b464cc` from [Velo #90](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/velo/pull/90), update all three lockfiles, and expose Velo metrics through Dynamo.

All four modes use the same frozen UCX-enabled binary and 2,048 speedup-10 mock workers. All 16 measured runs are retained: 9,854,326 completed exported records, including five empty-content errors.

Velo TCP delivered 66.5% more output tokens/s than TCP, with 21.6% less frontend CPU/request and 46.6% fewer RX packets/output token. QUIC had the best throughput, CPU/request, and packet cost. Velo RDMA showed no clear throughput gain over Velo TCP and used 16.5% more combined wire packets/output token. Velo improved p99 TTFT against TCP but increased p99 per-request mean ITL. The report separates fabric differences, client limits, and TCP drain cancellations. These are directional results; defaults are unchanged.

Maximum worker-process occupancy was 601 slots without admission backpressure, so this did not reproduce the historical concentration of 5,760 streams on one peer. The bounded-admission unit test passed separately.
- Four repeats per mode completed on normal, non-preemptible Tyche allocations with the same five nodes; no backfill. All exports and KV-source checks passed, with no silent TCP fallback in RDMA runs. Small request errors were retained. The report records 6,236 TCP drain cancellations separately and includes all provisional limits; p99 per-request mean ITL exceeds its limit against TCP for QUIC and both Velo modes.

title: feat(runtime): start every discovery watch with one resync snapshot
body:
Fixes #15066. Follow-up to #14769.

## Summary

Every `Discovery::list_and_watch` stream now starts with the state at establishment as one
`Added` event per matching instance and then exactly one `DiscoveryEvent::Resync` of the same
set, empty when nothing matches. A consumer that reopens a watch after losing one replaces its
state with that `Resync` and needs no `list()` call; an instance that left during the gap is
absent from the snapshot.

Design decision: the initial `Added` events stay, and the `Resync` follows them. Every existing
consumer either replaces its state on `Resync` with a set it already holds (no double-count, no
republish) or ignores `Resync`.

Per backend:

- **KV stores (etcd, file, memory):** `Bucket::watch` sends the existing entries as one
  `WatchEvent::Resync` instead of a `Put` burst, so the discovery layer's existing resync
  translation ends the startup burst with the snapshot. The discovery stream,
  `TypedPrefixWatcher`, and `KvCache` log the first resync at debug and a later one at warn. The
  NATS store is not a discovery backend and keeps its `Put` replay.
- **Kubernetes:** the daemon reports `Pending`/`Ready`/`Stopped`/`Failed` on a watch channel and
  sends `Ready` only after both reflectors completed their initial list and the result is in
  `list_state`. `list_and_watch` and `list` wait for `Ready` and fail when the daemon stopped or
  failed first, instead of returning an empty set the caller cannot tell from an empty cluster.
  The wait is unbounded while a reflector retries its initial list (unreachable API server, RBAC
  denial); the trait doc states this. `list_and_watch` stops waiting when the caller's
  cancellation token fires. `list()` waiting for readiness is a deliberate change to a second
  method, for consistency with the watch.
- **Mock:** one `Resync` after the `Added` burst.

Consumer audit (every `list_and_watch` caller in `lib/` and `lib/bindings/python`):

- Replace-on-`Resync`, unchanged set: `component/client.rs` (`EndpointDiscoverySource`),
  `llm/discovery/controller.rs` (revision-guarded), `llm/kv_dc_relay/discovery.rs`
  (`replace_all` reports no change), `llm/discovery/runtime_configs.rs` (no republish).
- Ignore `Resync`: `llm/discovery/{endpoint_card,kv_source_watch,watcher}.rs`,
  `llm/direct_zmq_fan_in.rs`, `llm/kv_router/indexer/recovery/{direct_zmq,state_agent}.rs`,
  `llm/kv_router/publisher/state_agent_host.rs`, `runtime/discovery/utils.rs`,
  `runtime/pipeline/network/egress/push_router.rs`,
  `runtime/transports/event_plane/dynamic_subscriber.rs`, `bindings/python/rust/llm/fpm.rs`.
- Re-list on every event: `llm/kv_router/publisher/attachment_owner.rs` and
  `llm/kv_dc_relay/membership_watch.rs` do one extra `list()` per new watch at startup. Benign.

Out of scope, for follow-up issues: `push_router.rs` watchers reconnect on stream end but keep
their dispatch and indexer state and ignore `Resync`, so the new snapshot does not yet remove an
instance that left during their gap; a Kubernetes watch opened before a post-`Ready` daemon
failure keeps serving and never errors (pre-existing, now observable through `DaemonState`).

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p dynamo-runtime --tests -- -D warnings` at every
  commit, `cargo clippy -p dynamo-llm --no-default-features --tests -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo test -p dynamo-runtime --lib`: 825 passed. `cargo test -p dynamo-llm
  --no-default-features --lib -- runtime_configs kv_dc_relay::discovery`: 23 passed.
- The shared startup contract (`discovery::startup_contract`) runs against the memory, file, and
  mock backends in two cases. An empty registry gives one empty `Resync`. A populated one gives
  its `Added` events and one `Resync` of the complete set, and a registration, a model taint
  update, and a removal made right after `list_and_watch` returns all follow that snapshot, which
  still holds the pre-change state.
- The Kubernetes stream is checked against a cluster-less client: the initial set, then one
  `Resync`, then later changes; a pending daemon holding the watch until `Ready` or
  cancellation; a stopped or failed daemon failing `list` and `list_and_watch`. The daemon test
  checks that `Ready` waits for both initial lists and follows the `list_state` write. The etcd
  store's initial `Resync` has a live-etcd test.
- Reconnect: a consumer replaces its state on the first `Resync` of a fresh stream.
  `a_resync_replaces_the_instances_of_a_discovery_source` covers replacement, and the contract
  tests prove each backend's snapshot content.
- Mutation check: dropping the startup `Resync` on memory, file, mock, and Kubernetes, letting
  readiness follow one initial list, and removing the cancellation race each turn a test red.

title: fix(runtime): cache configured etcd lease TTL once per process
body:
## Overview:

Read the existing `ETCD_LEASE_TTL` environment setting once per process using `OnceLock`, so runtime/component clients consistently request the same configured default. Preserve explicit builder overrides and the existing 10-second fallback for unset or invalid values; keep renewal cadence based on the granted lease.

## Details:

Cache only the environment-derived default TTL. Clients using that default share the cached value even after the environment changes; explicit `ClientOptions::lease_ttl` or builder overrides may request different TTLs. The documentation now states this distinction in both configuration and transport code.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/runtime/src/transports/etcd.rs`: `LEASE_TTL_SECS`, `default_lease_ttl`, `resolve_lease_ttl`, and the unit/integration tests for caching and explicit overrides.
- `lib/runtime/src/config/environment_names.rs`: the `ETCD_LEASE_TTL` configuration contract.

## Related Issues

- Relates to #12312: completes the requested once-per-process configuration behavior.
- Relates to #8076: the environment variable was introduced there.

## Overview:

Adds three temporary pre-merge lanes (`vllm-gb300-test`, `sglang-gb300-test`, `trtllm-gb300-test`) that exercise the `aws-gb300-tester-arm-gpu-v2` ARM64 runner pool against real test workloads, so the pool can be validated before these lanes move to `nightly-ci.yml`. ## Details:

Supporting changes in `.github/workflows/shared-test.yml`:

- `arm_runner` is now an input (default `prod-tester-arm-v2`) rather than a hardcoded literal in `runs-on`, so a lane can target a different ARM pool.
- GPU-test gating moves from a hardcoded `matrix.platform == 'amd64'` to `contains(fromJSON(inputs.gpu_test_platforms), matrix.platform)`, defaulting to `'["amd64"]'`. This stays separate from `platform` on purpose: several existing lanes deliberately include `arm64` in `platform` for CPU coverage while running that entry on a GPU-less ARM runner, so GPU gating cannot be derived from `platform`.
- `amd_runner` becomes optional with a default, since the new arm64-only lanes never read it.
- A `models_dir` input is threaded through to the `pytest-local` action as `--models-dir`, letting a lane use a pre-populated model cache instead of downloading models online.

The GB300 lanes use 120 minutes per GPU stage. Both the parallel and sequential stages each receive `gpu_test_timeout_minutes`, so twice that value must stay under GitHub's 360-minute default job timeout; overrunning it cancels the job mid-stage and reports no results at all.

title: feat(sidecar): speak TensorRT-LLM's OpenEngine gRPC API
body:
## Summary

TensorRT-LLM is adding OpenEngine (`openengine.v1`) as its gRPC surface. This migrates `lib/sidecar/trtllm` off the bespoke `TrtllmService` protocol and adds disaggregated serving, which the old protocol had no representation for.

**Vendored protos, not the BSR.** The Buf Schema Registry Rust SDK needs a per-developer token to build — a bad first-run experience — and it pinned this crate to a different tonic version than the rest of the workspace. The protos are vendored instead, with `proto/README.md` recording the upstream commit and a SHA-256 per file so the copies stay verifiable.

**Disaggregation follows the protocol's own shape.** A prefill worker marks its request `context_only` through `extra` and terminates with `PrefillReady` instead of `finished`; the decode worker replays the returned `KvSessionRef` verbatim. The handoff is opaque JSON, so `disagg.rs` owns the codec and refuses anything it cannot round-trip — non-finite numbers, integers past 2^53, a missing endpoint port.

**Shared JSON codec.** `json.rs` moves from the vLLM sidecar into `dynamo-sidecar-common`, since both sidecars now need Struct↔JSON conversion. Behaviour and error text are unchanged.

## Notable details

- The prefill leg's synthesized terminal chunk uses `FinishReason::Length`. The frontend's prefill router treats any other terminal reason as "already complete" and never runs the decode leg.
- `Control.GetModelInfo` is called once at startup for the model's context length; `--context-length` supplies it when the engine reports none, which is what an engine started without `--max_seq_len` does.
- Cancellation closes the stream and issues `Control.Abort`.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p dynamo-trtllm-sidecar -p dynamo-vllm-sidecar -p dynamo-sidecar-common` — all green (26 sidecar tests, 2 ignored real-engine E2E hooks).
- `cargo clippy --workspace`, `cargo fmt --all`, and the full pre-commit suite pass.
- End-to-end against a real TensorRT-LLM engine (1.3.0rc25, Qwen3-0.6B, RTX 5880 Ada) through the Dynamo frontend: aggregated and disaggregated, streaming, logprobs, and guided decoding with `xgrammar`. Disaggregated runs confirmed genuinely split — the frontend logged distinct `prefill_worker_id` and `decode_worker_id` — over the NIXL cache transceiver.
- Concurrent requests (6/6) and client-cancellation paths exercised by hand.

Review round, measured against a local build of TensorRT-LLM main at `8bbaf66bd5`, the commit that introduced the OpenEngine servicer. (The build's in-tree version string reads `1.3.0rc26`, but the published `v1.3.0rc26` tree does not carry the servicer — the commit is the meaningful identifier.)

- `openengine-target-dp-rank` is rejected with `UNIMPLEMENTED` at every rank, including 0, as is `openengine-priority`; a request carrying neither succeeds. The sidecar now refuses a rank hint in `validate_request` rather than letting the engine fail it.
- An engine started without `--max_seq_len` answers `GetModelInfo` with `max_context_length` **unset** — it does not substitute a placeholder. Docs corrected accordingly.
- `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` is emitted nowhere in the installed `tensorrt_llm`; `ERROR_CODE_OVERLOADED` has a single emitter, the consumer-stall watchdog. Both mappings changed to match.

Re-validated on the published release `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc27.dev202609170000`, the first public tag carrying the OpenEngine servicer (TinyLlama-1.1B, RTX 5880 Ada, through the Dynamo frontend).

- **Aggregated:** non-streaming chat, 25-chunk SSE stream, `/v1/completions` with `logprobs=2` (`token_logprobs` and `top_logprobs` both populated), and a request omitting `max_tokens` served from the registered context window.
- **Disaggregated:** the same four requests over the NIXL cache transceiver, with `KvCacheTransceiverV2 ... TransferWorker ready` on both engines and the prefill and decode sidecars each logging all four — zero warnings on either.
- **The three contract claims reproduce exactly.** `openengine-target-dp-rank` (ranks 0 and 3) and `openengine-priority` both return `UNIMPLEMENTED`, while the same request without metadata succeeds; `GetModelInfo` reports `max_context_length` unset for an engine started without `--max_seq_len`, whose own args log `max_input_len=1024 max_seq_len=None`; and statically, `ERROR_CODE_OVERLOADED` has one emitter (`servicer.py:241`), `RESPONSE_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0` (`streaming.py:27`), the rank/priority rejection sits at `request_mapping.py:189`, and `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` appears in zero files. `control.py:258` now states it outright: `supports_priority = False  # Generate rejects openengine-priority`.
- A dp-rank hint reaches the sidecar's guard and fails as `InvalidRequest: data-parallel rank targeting is not supported by the TensorRT-LLM sidecar` instead of a 5xx out of the engine.
- The release ships the servicer but **not** the `openengine.v1` bindings it imports, so a stock image exits with `Failed to import OpenEngine support: No module named 'openengine'`. The docs, launch script, and manifest now name the release as the floor and keep the pinned pip step (the pins resolve cleanly against its protobuf 6.33.6).

## Follow-up

title: fix(ci): harden DGDR profiling against disk pressure
body:
## Summary

- add explicit CPU, memory, and ephemeral-storage requests to the DGDR CI `profiler` and `output-copier` containers so they are no longer `BestEffort`
- bound profiler ephemeral storage with container limits and `profiling-output.emptyDir.sizeLimit`
- set `backoffLimit: 1` so an evicted profiling Pod gets one clean retry that can be scheduled away from a node under `DiskPressure`
- preserve explicit per-test overrides and the existing Hugging Face token injection

The selected values are intentionally conservative for the mocker-based CPU suite: the profiler requests `250m` CPU, `512Mi` memory, and `1Gi` ephemeral storage with a `4Gi` ephemeral-storage limit; the output copier requests `25m` CPU, `64Mi` memory, and `128Mi` ephemeral storage with a `256Mi` limit. The shared output volume is capped at `1Gi`. CPU and memory limits remain unset to avoid adding throttling or OOM failure modes.

`backoffLimit: 1` recreates the Pod after an eviction; it is not live migration. A node carrying the `DiskPressure` taint should be avoided by the replacement Pod, although Kubernetes does not guarantee that every retry lands on a different node.

## Observed CI impact
